original.description: Objective:To characterise spacecraft materials that minimise atmospheric impacts during re-entry.Description:ESA's Green Agendaand Ecodesign Policy require that the environmental impacts of all space missions andprogrammes are assessed and reduced across their full life cycle. Launch and spacecraft re-entry effects onthe atmosphere are known gaps to fulfil these requirements. This results in significant uncertainty andsystematic exclusion of such effects when developing materials on the basis of sustainable performance.Previous and ongoing Discovery activities, Insights into the Chemistry of Atmospheric Re-entry of JunkedSpacecraft (ICARUS) and Impacts of space Debris ablation on Earth's Atmospheric System (IDEAS), havehighlighted the potential importance of ablation products in the atmosphere while established initial modellingapproaches and experimental validation capabilities.The proposed activity addresses this critical knowledge gap by developing a consolidated experimental andmodelling framework to characterise emissionsfrom spacecraft re-entry and integrate these into atmosphericand design assessment tools. This will enable the incorporation of atmospheric impacts into Life CycleAssessment (LCA) and support both Ecodesign and Design-for-Demise (D4D) decision making. Such aframework would be the first worldwide.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify representative launcher and spacecraftdemise-critical materials as well as Space Debris Particles(SPSs)- Propose material characterization factors (e.g. Ozon Depletionmetrics, radiative forcing proxies) andassociated quantification methodology- Refine methods to allow observation and characterization of particles generated during the vaporizationphase of selected materials- Demonstrate validation tests under realistic atmospheric re-entry conditions (e.g. Thermal, pressure andflow conditions) measuring and linking ablation fluxes to downstream chemical compositions- Parametrization and modelling of datasets for integration into re-entry and atmospheric chemistryclimatemodels-Define uncertainty and applicability ranges for model use- Formulate recommendations for standardised testing procedures to support the continuous developmentand population of material datasets.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME  RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. original.description: Objective: To develop an Electro-Dynamic-Shield system to mitigate systems degradation for missions to the Moon, Mars and planetarybodies including a significant dusty environment.Description: Exploration systems in contact with planetary surfaces covered in regolith such as the Moon and Mars are subject to local dust displacement and accumulation on critical surfaces affecting system performance as for instance thermal balance, power generation efficiency and optical transmission and system lifetime. A number of mitigation strategies have been put forward and tested mostly on ground with a very limited demonstration in space. The Electro-Dynamic Shield (EDS) technology is a method used to mitigate the accumulation of dust on surfaces, particularly in space environments. This technology employs electric fields to repel dust particles, preventing them from settling on critical surfaces such as solar panels, sensors, and other equipment. This technology has been studied for more than twenty years outside of Europe for the mitigation of dust deposition on terrestrial and space system and it has been recently demonstrated on the Moon. In Europe, most of the studies performed so far have been on laboratory scale. Among others, an experimental EDS was successfully implemented on a number of samples including optical glass and Kapton sheets and demonstrated very high dust removal efficiency in a vacuum environment including UV, showing good potential for targeted system feasibility studies. Based on this success, the feasibility of implementing such technology on actual space hardware by breadboarding and testing critical functionalities can be addressed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define the requirements for the implementation of an EDS system into relevant spacecraft structures and materials of interest with a priority towards solar arrays (with possible applicability to optical surface and other materials) and define the requirements from the target system towards EDS. - Assess the required modifications of standard designs to accommodate an EDS system, establish a list of technological gaps, define specific tests and a test plan to address the technological gaps. - Design and manufacture relevant breadboards to demonstrate EDS operational efficiency on targeted system. - Perform test for critical functionalities,including in representative laboratory environments (dusty vacuum and in presence of UV). - Based on the tests outcomes and future missions needs provide a technical roadmap with a cost outline.

original.description: Objective: The objective is to develop, implement and test Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) on the uplink of a Beyond 5G (B5G)satellite system. The link shall be representative of3GPP-compliant Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) scenarios .TargetedImprovements:Improving resources utilisation in dense and / or heterogenous system environments, allowing 50% spectral efficiency increase withrespect to orthogonal multiple access.Description: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is recognized as a key technology for beyond 5G networks, aiming to enhance the system capacity and tackle the challenges ofmassive connectivity by improving spectrum efficiency. NOMA was studied in 3GPP release 15 for New Radio (NR) in TN context but it was not pursued. Instead, it wasclassified as a technology for next generation. However, only Code-Domain NOMA was analysed in release 15. Since then, both academia and major industry players havebeen working on enhancing NOMA, including both Code-Domain (CD-NOMA) and Power-Domain (PD-NOMA) variants and they have yielded promising results including NTNscenarios up to 80% throughput gain. Among the challenges that these efforts have targeted are implementation complexity and interference management.This activity will develop and test over-the-air an efficient and low complexity NOMA techniques for satellite uplink using 3GPP NR NTN air interface. The developments concernboth the strategy for poweror code allocation and user pairing, as well as the efficient implementation of successive interference cancellation at the receiver. User pairing andpower allocation shall consider both a distributed grant-free AI-based strategy such as a distributed leaning methodology with an agent at each user, and a static strategy basedon the network architecture. The implementation of Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) at the receiver side shall consider the receiver processing chain based on 3GPPair interface. The selected NOMA solution shall be compared to a benchmark orthogonal multiple access scheme in the specified scenarios and use cases considering as aminimum the system throughput, latency and complexity. Furthermore, the outcome of the activity shall serve as a benchmark for beyond 5G standardization. The integration ofNOMA in beyond 5G shall be seen either as stand-alone access scheme (for massiveconnectivity scenarios for example), or opportunistic on top of orthogonal access when thelatter is not able to serve all users (sudden user population peaks or specific heterogenous systems).

original.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design and test an engineering model of a Direct Sampling Radio Unit (DSRU) covering the 5G frequency bands FR1 and FR2.TargetedImprovements:Enabling direct sampling of all 5G frequency bands, providing an RF front end and Digital Signal Processing chip to achieve flexible 5G NTN communication with 20%reduction in power consumption compared to the current state of the art.Description: Current RF Systems-on-Chip (SoC) enables direct sampling in Frequency Range 1 (FR1), but higher frequency ranges still require down-conversion stages to sample atbaseband. There is a significant market need for a solution that enables direct sampling across all 5G frequency bands, simplifying the system architecture and improving theefficiency of5G Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN). As payload capacity and re-configuration requirements increase, the conventional functions - such as separate analoguereceiver / transmitter, filtering and DSP - become more complex, power hungry and with a time to market which is not suitable for a fast-moving NTN scenario. To address thesechallenges, direct RF sampling with wide bandwidth and software-defined architecture offer a simple, scalable, and efficient solution. It supports flexible frequency planning,reduces filtering requirements and enables higher modulation schemes for higher throughput. In addition, integrated DSP enables agile frequency tuning, on-chip digital signalprocessing, and clock for multichip synchronization. Integrated digital signal processing will support the transition to software-defined radio payloads, creating a highlyconfigurable, common hardware / software device that can be used in next generation of communication satellites.This activity will identify discrete Commercial-of-The-Shelf (COTS) ADC / DAC or mixed-signal chips capable of direct sampling of Frequency Range 2 (FR 2), covering both KuandKa-Band. An engineering model of a Direct Sampling Radio Unit (DSRU) covering the 5G frequency bands FR1 and FR will be designed and manufactured. original.description: The Copernicus Sentinel-2 Next Generation space component, which is the subject of this procurement, will ensure a seamless continuation of the current Sentinel-2 first generation capabilities, whilst increasing both the quantity and quality of the products. The development of the Sentinel-2 Next Generation (Sentinel-2 NG) Space Component aims to build upon and enhance the initial observations provided by the first generation. In particular, Sentinel-2 NG (S2NG) will respond to the needs of Copernicus Services, with particular emphasis to the Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) and the Emergency Management Service (CEMS), together with, as secondary objective, the Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS). This will be characterised by enhanced spatial sampling and spectral sampling compared to Sentinel-2 first generation. S2 NG will provide observations for the next generation of operational products such as landcover maps, land-change detection maps, and geophysical properties,  together with, as secondary objective, for the next generation of operational products over a larger portion of coastal and marine waters compared to Sentinel-2. S2NG will provide quantitative evidence in support to European and global policies, including the Green Deal, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the EU Forest Strategy, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, the EU Soil Strategy, the EU Water Framework and the UN SDGs. The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. Each satellite will embark a payload comprised of the Advanced Multi-Spectral Imager (AMSI) instrument with two detection chains, one for Visible and Near-Infrared (VNIR) detection and one for the Short Wavelength Infrared (SWIR) detection, with a total of 21 bands (16 in VNIR, 5 in SWIR).The ITT for the Sentinel-2 NG Phases B2/C/D/E1 is in open competition. The ITTwill cover all spacecraft development phases (B2/C/D/E1) of the complete Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft (i.e. including Payload and Spacecraft subsystems), and the Model B Spacecraft the latter through a contractual mandatory option. This ITT will be arranged in two Contractual Phases as follows: Phase 1 will include:  - all Payload Instruments activities up to the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Instrument Preliminary Design Review, and subsequent payload advanced phase C activities up to the end of the satellite Phase B2 (PDR);- all Sentinel-2 NG spacecraft activities, including the System Requirements Review (SRR), up to and including the Satellite Preliminary Design Review (PDR); and - the procurement of relevant long lead Items (LLI) for both Sentinel-2 NG Model A and Model B Spacecraft. Phase 2 will include: - All remaining Spacecraft activities up to and including the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft Qualification and Flight Acceptance Review (QAR).Additional information: The Invitation to Tender (ITT) will be published on ESA Star. In order to access the ITT Package, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as potential ESA suppliers. Any Tenderer, which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier, must complete the online questionnaire in esa-star, https://esastar-emr.sso. esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found in ESA's INDUSTRY PORTAL available at: - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/esa-star_open_for_business - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/How_to_do/esa-star_Registration_Process Please note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESA contracts requires "Full" registration.
